record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: Why is the CE charge-ordered state in manganites so sensitive to low levels of Cr doping, and can that extreme sensitivity be reproduced in unbiased Monte Carlo simulations of realistic models?

evidence.quote: Why is the CE-state so sensitive to Cr-doping? ... Can this be reproduced in MC simulations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider doped manganite compounds of the form R_{1-x}A_x MnO_3 (with R a rare earth and A a divalent cation) near half doping x ≈ 1/2, where the so-called CE phase is observed: a charge-ordered, orbital-ordered, antiferromagnetic insulating state with checkerboard ordering of nominal Mn^{3+}/Mn^{4+} sites and zig-zag ferromagnetic chains coupled antiferromagnetically. Experimentally, substituting a small percentage (a few percent) of Mn ions by Cr ions is known to rapidly destroy the CE state and induce ferromagnetic metallic behavior with colossal magnetoresistance.

Within a realistic microscopic model of manganites that includes two e_g orbitals, double-exchange coupling of itinerant electrons to localized t_{2g} core spins, antiferromagnetic superexchange between t_{2g} spins, and cooperative Jahn–Teller electron–phonon coupling (with optional quenched disorder), modeled on a two- or three-dimensional lattice with a fraction y of Mn sites replaced by Cr-like impurities (e.g. sites that lack e_g orbitals and carry an S = 3/2 core spin coupled antiferromagnetically to neighbors):

(a) Provide a mechanism that explains why the CE charge/orbital-ordered insulating phase of the undoped (y = 0) model is destabilized by an infinitesimal or very small impurity concentration y, in contrast to the relative robustness expected for a long-range-ordered ground state to dilute impurities.

(b) Demonstrate, via unbiased Monte Carlo simulations of this model (treating core spins classically and integrating out fermions exactly at each sweep, or an equivalent unbiased scheme), that the CE phase is destroyed and a competing ferromagnetic metallic state is stabilized at small y, quantitatively reproducing the experimentally observed extreme sensitivity of the CE state to Cr doping.
artifact.status_search_result: Follow-up Monte Carlo studies of half-doped manganite models with disorder and Jahn–Teller phonons (e.g., Aliaga et al., Phys. Rev. B 68, 104405 (2003); cond-mat/0303513) demonstrated the fragility of the CE phase to quenched disorder and the resulting CMR phenomenology, providing substantial theoretical support for the mechanism. Subsequent work on A-site disorder confirms CO melting without applied field. However, a fully quantitative reproduction matching the extreme experimental sensitivity to Cr-specific substitution is not definitively established, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Theoretical study of half-doped models for manganites: Fragility of CE phase with disorder
status_evidence.snippet: Monte Carlo study showing CE phase is fragile to disorder, with competing FM metallic state and CMR.
status_evidence.claim: Unbiased MC simulations reproduce CE-phase fragility to disorder, supporting the proposed mechanism.

status_evidence.title: Mixed exchange interactions: Cr doped manganites
status_evidence.snippet: Cr dilutes double-exchange FM and promotes AFM superexchange via Cr3+/Mn4+ ions.
status_evidence.claim: Cr doping locally alters exchange pathways, contributing to CE destabilization.

status_evidence.title: Field induced melting of charge order in manganites (thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Strong A-site disorder destroys CO even without applied field in MC simulations.
status_evidence.claim: Disorder-driven destruction of charge order is established via Monte Carlo simulations.
